summary.headline: Gland Pharma Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22% to INR17,428 million with a 30% adjusted EBITDA margin; FY27 guided to 12–13% constant-currency growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered record quarterly revenue and EBITDA, led by Dalbavancin launch, tender wins, and new CDMO products, with Cenexi back to positive EBITDA (EUR1 million in Q4). Full-year revenue grew 14.5% to INR64,307 million, adjusted EBITDA margin rose 360 bps to 26%, and adjusted PAT margin reached 16%. Base business (ex-Cenexi) EBITDA margin was 41% in Q4 and 38% for FY26. Management guided FY27 consolidated growth of 12–13% at constant currency, excluding any GLP-1 upside, and a 15% CAGR over the next four years.

segments.name: United States
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR9,716 million (+26% YoY); FY26 INR33,181 million (+11%). 31 products launched in FY26, including 5 in Q4; 24 ANDAs filed and 28 approvals received.

segments.name: Europe and other regulated markets
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR794 million; FY26 INR3,249 million (+11%), supported by the integrated business development model.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,468 million (+17%); FY26 INR6,511 million (+7%). Management said Saudi Arabia shipments were paused, hurting Q4 ROW sequentially; ROW is 2–3% of sales.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR670 million; FY26 INR2,672 million.

segments.name: Cenexi
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue EUR45 million (+4% YoY); FY26 revenue EUR182 million (+11%), with EBITDA improved by EUR16 million. Profitable in Q3 and Q4 FY26; Q4 EBITDA EUR1 million. Target of mid-to-high single-digit EBITDA margin by end-FY27 and mid-teen EBITDA medium term.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: 46% of group revenue and +28% growth in FY26 (Cenexi is 100% CDMO). Base business CDMO is 23% of base revenue, growing 33%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 12–13% on a constant-currency basis, excluding GLP-1 and FX upside; management cited about USD40–50 million of incremental CDMO growth and about INR650 crore from base business plus about INR150 crore from Cenexi.
Cenexi FY27 revenue target of close to EUR200 million, with most growth expected in FY28; EBITDA target of at least mid-to-high single digit by end of FY27.
Base business EBITDA margin guided at 33–35% for FY27; consolidated EBITDA margin around 25–26%.
Consolidated revenue CAGR of about 15% over the next four years; FY28 guided at around 15%, with a step-up in FY29 (about 19–20%+) as complex products launch.
GLP-1 volumes and approvals excluded from guidance; treated as upside. Partner approvals expected in FY27, with some launches from Q3 FY27.
Tax rate expected to decline as Cenexi profitability improves (FY26 ETR about 29%).
capex_capacity: Capex plan of about INR2,000 crore over the next 3 years on top of about INR300 crore in FY26; about INR500 crore expected in FY27. Investments cover ophthalmic suspension line, blow-fill-seal technology (next year), and CDMO dedicated lines.
GLP-1 cartridge capacity at 140 million units; insulin vial and cartridge fills may occupy 30–40 million units over the next couple of years until GLP-1 ramp-up around 2030.
Two new lines commissioned in Q4 FY26 at the Indian base business, one more to go live next quarter.
Cenexi Fontenay ampoule line adds 30 million ampoule capacity by 2027; replacement line to be put in place this summer (August).
Cenexi utilisation: Fontenay near 100%, Osny solid orals about 90%, two other sites at 50–60%.
Acquired a solar plant in India to reduce power costs.
demand_pricing: Dalbavancin launched in the US and Europe in Feb–Mar 2026 with strong demand; Vizient contract won, and management said there was no channel stuffing in Q4.
Multivitamin (MVI) approval received in April 2026, launch expected in the current quarter, with steady revenue contribution.
Three to four recently launched products plus a GPO contract were said to contribute about USD40 million in FY27.
Increased demand for existing products from competitively priced contract wins, aided by procurement cost programs and economies of scale.
Cenexi: 5–6 products signed with Cenexi's own clientele; 3 MAs signed for Cenexi to act as a releasing entity in Europe.
Cenexi won a large hormonal drug contract in prefilled syringes with a European laboratory.
GLP-1: 8 contracts signed, 6–7 more expected soon; CDMO for liraglutide, semaglutide and tirzepatide; no specific volumes or approvals disclosed.

Raw-material and packaging: solvent delays reported; glass and vial suppliers seeking 5–6% price increases, with a possible 1–2% overall margin impact; logistics cost impact on revenue of 1–2%, shared with partners.

qa_highlights.question: Is Cenexi EBITDA-neutral in FY27 at EUR45 million quarterly revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets at least mid-to-high single-digit EBITDA for Cenexi by end-FY27, driven by efficiencies and higher-value product mix rather than revenue scale.

qa_highlights.question: Can Cenexi revenue exceed EUR200 million in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said close to EUR200 million is the FY27 target, with most growth in FY28 when the new ampoule line is commercialised.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 12–13% guidance conservative given FX tailwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is on constant currency; any FX movement is treated as upside. Q4 constant-currency growth and US growth were not disclosed and will be followed up separately.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 140 million unit GLP-1 capacity is contracted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify contracted capacity, which depends on partner projections; announcements would follow partner approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Why was capacity expanded for GLP-1 before demand is clear?
qa_highlights.answer: The new line is a combo vial and cartridge line, with insulin contracts filling it until GLP-1 ramp-up around 2030 (insulin may use 30–40 million units).

qa_highlights.question: Why did Gland acquire Cenexi, and what is its utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Rationale includes European CDMO entry, MA releasing entity, hormone and controlled-substance capabilities; Fontenay near 100%, Osny about 90%, two sites at 50–60%.

risks_watch: GLP-1 timing: no approvals, volumes or contracted capacity disclosed; partner approvals expected in FY27 and launches from Q3 FY27 or later.
Rest of World (Saudi Arabia) shipments paused in Q4, with a recovery hoped for next quarter.
Input cost pressure: glass and vial price increases of 5–6%, possible 1–2% margin impact; solvent delays; logistics impact of 1–2% of revenue.
Q4 one-off milestone and profit-share income (9% and 6% of revenue, as per the management reply) may affect the margin quality.
Leadership: CEO search is active, with a preference for candidates with CDMO and biologics background.
Currency: Q4 constant-currency growth not disclosed; FX gains contributed to other income of INR1,115 million in Q4.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the base business, CDMO pipeline and Cenexi turnaround, but deliberately conservative in guidance by excluding GLP-1 and FX. Management was evasive on GLP-1 contracted volumes, approvals and constant-currency growth, citing partner confidentiality and volatility.
key_quotes: It has been a very strong quarter and a year for us in terms of revenues and profitability.
So anything which happens on GLP-1 will be an upside.
I am pleased to share that we have reported highest ever quarterly revenues and EBITDA during fourth quarter of FY '26.
